title: OpenID Connect

searches.query: "OpenID Connect" interview ID token access token nonce account linking
searches.result: success; exact-concept search executed, but independent frequency/rank/company evidence was insufficient; prompts are original production adaptations and technical decisions use checked primary sources

sources.title: System Design Primer: Security
sources.supportRationale: Core conceptual orientation checked during specification; its brief section explicitly needs updates and is not the sole protocol/crypto authority or evidence of interview frequency.

sources.title: OpenID Connect Core 1.0 incorporating errata set 2
sources.supportRationale: Identity layer, ID Token and flow-specific issuer/audience/nonce validation; logout/discovery details need their own verified extension contract if used.

sources.title: OpenID Connect Discovery 1.0
sources.supportRationale: Trusted issuer metadata, issuer consistency and key discovery; endpoints are not selected from an arbitrary untrusted token.

sources.title: OpenID Connect RP-Initiated Logout 1.0
sources.supportRationale: Explicit relying-party initiated logout protocol, separate from local session cleanup and access-token revocation; no unsupported global logout guarantee.

sources.title: IETF RFC 8725: JSON Web Token Best Current Practices
sources.supportRationale: Algorithm verification, trusted keys, issuer/audience and distinct JWT usage profiles; not a universal authorization or revocation protocol.

sources.title: OWASP: Authorization Cheat Sheet
sources.supportRationale: Least privilege, default denial and resource/action authorization on every request, with trusted enforcement and failure handling.

sources.title: OWASP: Authentication Cheat Sheet
sources.supportRationale: Identity proof, reauthentication, safe responses and protection of authentication endpoints; deployment-specific choices remain explicit.

sources.title: IETF RFC 9700: OAuth 2.0 Security Best Current Practice
sources.supportRationale: Modern OAuth threat model, redirects, PKCE, client-specific refresh-token replay protection and scoped revocation concerns.

sources.title: IETF RFC 7636: Proof Key for Code Exchange
sources.supportRationale: Per-authorization-request verifier/challenge binding and supported exchange validation; distinct from arbitrary API proof of possession.

sources.title: OWASP: Session Management Cheat Sheet
sources.supportRationale: Opaque session lifecycle, cookie scope, regeneration, expiry and server-side invalidation; flags do not replace authorization/CSRF controls.

scenarios.theme: A gateway accepts any valid ID Token for API calls. What changes?
scenarios.assumptions: Tokens may be intended for several relying parties and carry no API-specific authority. What will you do and why?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies OpenID Connect to api id token.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: A gateway accepts any valid ID Token for API calls. What changes?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Validate the API’s intended access-token profile/audience and resource policy, while the login client separately validates its own ID Tokens.

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: Issuer/client configuration adds work

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: Shared signing keys do not make tokens for different recipients and purposes interchangeable.

evidence.rationale: Primary support mapped to oidc, jwt, authz; interview frequency is not claimed.

full-delivery.rationale: Three labeled parts are self-contained; native disclosure and host confidence integration use stable keys.

scenarios.theme: A request supplies a new issuer URL and asks to trust its keys. Is discovery enough?
scenarios.assumptions: The service has not onboarded or authorized that provider. What will you do and why?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies OpenID Connect to arbitrary issuer.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: A request supplies a new issuer URL and asks to trust its keys. Is discovery enough?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Restrict discovery to the configured trusted issuer/client relationship and enforce issuer/metadata consistency with bounded retrieval

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: Provider onboarding is less automatic

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: HTTPS transport to an attacker-controlled issuer proves its connection, not the application’s trust in its identities.

evidence.rationale: Primary support mapped to discovery, oidc; interview frequency is not claimed.

full-delivery.rationale: Three labeled parts are self-contained; native disclosure and host confidence integration use stable keys.

scenarios.theme: A new provider returns the same email as an existing administrator. Merge automatically?
scenarios.assumptions: The user has not proven control of the existing local account. What will you do and why?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies OpenID Connect to email link.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: A new provider returns the same email as an existing administrator. Merge automatically?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Keep issuer/subject identity mapping distinct and require explicit appropriately authenticated account-linking proof before joining privileges.

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: More user steps reduce convenience

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: Even verified email has provider/reassignment semantics; blindly merging on text equality does not establish control of the old account.

evidence.rationale: Primary support mapped to oidc, authn; interview frequency is not claimed.

full-delivery.rationale: Three labeled parts are self-contained; native disclosure and host confidence integration use stable keys.

scenarios.theme: All users share one login nonce. What does the client need?
scenarios.assumptions: Callbacks can be replayed or associated with the wrong in-progress login. What will you do and why?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies OpenID Connect to nonce static.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: All users share one login nonce. What does the client need?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Use per-transaction SDK-managed binding and validate the flow-specific nonce/state/issuer and PKCE requirements instead of a static global value.

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: Transaction state needs expiry/cleanup

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: A nonce check cannot replace audience/signature checks, and PKCE is not a generic substitute for every OIDC response check.

evidence.rationale: Primary support mapped to oidc, bcp, pkce; interview frequency is not claimed.

full-delivery.rationale: Three labeled parts are self-contained; native disclosure and host confidence integration use stable keys.

scenarios.theme: An employee remains logged in at the provider after losing workspace membership. Can they enter?
scenarios.assumptions: Local organization access has been revoked even though external authentication succeeds. What will you do and why?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies OpenID Connect to local membership.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: An employee remains logged in at the provider after losing workspace membership. Can they enter?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Accept external identity only as identity, then deny absent current local membership/action permission under the workspace’s defined freshness policy.

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: Fresh local checks add dependencies

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: Provider SSO convenience and local authorization are separate; changing the provider account is not the only way to remove workspace access.

evidence.rationale: Primary support mapped to oidc, authz; interview frequency is not claimed.

full-delivery.rationale: Three labeled parts are self-contained; native disclosure and host confidence integration use stable keys.

scenarios.theme: Local logout succeeds but another relying party stays signed in. Is that unexpected?
scenarios.assumptions: The product claimed global logout without a configured cross-party protocol. What will you do and why?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies OpenID Connect to logout scope.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: Local logout succeeds but another relying party stays signed in. Is that unexpected?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Define local/provider/other-party/API token scope, implement supported logout mechanisms where required and test their actual propagation and failure behav

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: Federated logout adds protocol/state coordination and may be incomplete during failures

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: RP-Initiated Logout alone is not proof that every independent API token and session has vanished.

evidence.rationale: Primary support mapped to logout, session, oidc; interview frequency is not claimed.

full-delivery.rationale: Three labeled parts are self-contained; native disclosure and host confidence integration use stable keys.
